items.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: my dad used to bring home wonderful records like with Teddy Wilson and Benny Goodman, so that got me started, the Swing Era, you know the swing like Teddy.

ctx.x: Just move it and you can have it, right?

Because we couldn’t get it in the front door, we had to get a guy to bring it up through the window. It was one of those kind of things, in Connecticut. This was in Wallingford. So I started fooling around with the piano as well as taking my lessons on accordion, and then I started taking piano lessons in Connecticut at about the age of six. And every time I’d go over for a lesson she used to teach some of the students at Choate, the prep school there, it was right next to Choate. And so she said well you have to…
How did this piano teacher deal with your inclinations?
